mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 2.5% compresses discount rates in equity valuation models, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to increased present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% over the past 3 months signals monetary tightening, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (3-month average).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%) and low unemployment (UNRATE <= 4.0%) indicates a strong economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations for positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS <= 2.5% AND UNRATE <= 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, high housing starts (HOUST > 1300) signal overbuilding and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when the economy is in a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment level (PAYEMS increasing) signals expanding economic activity and stronger corporate earnings, which drives positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through improved investor sentiment.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105 over the past 3 months indicates weakening economic activity and reduced corporate output, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to lower earnings forecasts.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO < 105 (3-month average).

mechanism_narrative: A high housing market (HOUST > 1250) combined with weak industrial output (INDPRO < 108) reflects sectoral imbalance, leading to inflationary pressures and potential monetary tightening, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST > 1250 AND INDPRO < 108.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 255) triggers the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when CPIAUCSL > 255.
